findings.text: - s2 reconstructs each leaked call's parser input from the delivered argument in that run's `stream.jsonl` and tests that the parser, given that text, delivers exactly that argument; the delivered argument contains the census token `<｜DSML｜` by construction (that is how the census selected the call), so the test asserts a fixed point of the parser on text the delivered argument produced. It holds whether the parser leaked the token or the model wrote it into a string, and it fails only when the reconstruction is wrong, which the done-when gives no meaning to - so the twenty-call leg, stated as the per-leaked-call evidence, cannot discriminate the parser origin from the model origin it is weighed against - WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes - REASON: the twenty-call cross-check is the only per-leaked-call evidence the section offers, and as written it can never change the origin it is presented as settling.

- the chunking to be run is "chunks cut at the model's token boundaries", but no token set is named and none exists at hand: the model's tokenizer lives in the container `/work/projects/imas_gpu/containers/sglang-dev-dsv41.sif` under `/sgl-workspace`, so a worker must guess which tokenizer to load and whether its boundaries are the ones the serve produced. The done-when then requires the origin verdict to report findings "under any chunking", which makes an unreproducible chunking set load-bearing for the verdict - WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes - REASON: a differently-tokenized chunking set is a differently-scoped search, so the same parser could be named the origin or cleared depending on a choice the plan leaves free.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — census script and baseline log, `clive.py`, `router.py`/`RouterApp._relay`, `request_receipts.py`/`RequestReceipt`, the profile, the container `sif_path` and the census token `<｜DSML｜` all resolve as the plan describes them.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — s2's done-when names measurable results (the fixture directory's contents, a per-leaked-call delivery match, one named origin with its entry point and chunking) and declares a negative control that can fail: three clean completions through both entry points under every chunking must parse to their one call with no token in its argument.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the report and the new `fixtures/` tree are both declared write paths under the plan's own evidence directory, not a scratchpad; the sentence "Every log is written under the run directory" is loose wording, but the paths it names are durable and main-checkout-absolute.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s2 introduces no symbol, file or comment; the only names it adds are SGLang's own entry points, and no plan label or ticket reference reaches code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s2's per-leaked-call cross-check reconstructs the delivered argument from `stream.jsonl` and then tests the parser against that same text with the census token `<｜DSML｜` already inside it, so the check cannot separate the two origins it exists to separate.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s2 carries one deliverable, naming the layer the markup survives; the fig-07 question is now a single clause with §4 holding it when the origin differs from the one s2 reports, which an earlier review's answer folded in.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-declarations` marks s2 `implementable`, `plan-section-depends-on` wires s3 and s4 to `a-tool-call-carries-no-model-markup#s2`, and `plan-blocks` names `reckon:a-review-can-see-the-figure`; every target resolves.
